decisions.title: Enforce expiry both lazily and by a sweep
decisions.context: A join link must never admit anyone after its expiry, but a background sweep runs on a schedule and could lag.
options: Sweep only — a periodic job marks past-window invitations expired
Lazy only — treat a past expiresAt as expired on read
Both — lazy check for correctness, sweep to keep the table tidy
decisions.choice: Do both: evaluate expiry on read so correctness never depends on the sweep, and keep the sweep to move stale rows to the expired state.
decisions.tradeoffs: A little duplicated logic and one extra read-time check, in exchange for correctness that is independent of the sweep’s schedule.
decisions.consequence: A link is refused the instant it is past expiry, even if the sweep has not run yet.
decisions.author: agent

decisions.title: Accepting an invitation is idempotent
decisions.context: Recipients double-click links and email clients pre-fetch them, so an accept endpoint can be hit twice.
options: Create a membership per accept call
Create exactly one membership and treat later accepts as no-ops
decisions.choice: Accepting creates exactly one membership; a second accept on an already-accepted invitation changes nothing.
decisions.tradeoffs: Accept must re-check state inside the write, costing one guarded transaction, to rule out duplicate memberships.
decisions.consequence: Opening the join link twice can never place someone in the workspace twice.
decisions.author: agent

explanations.body: An admin adds a teammate by entering an email address and choosing one role; the system creates a pending invitation and emails a join link, so the teammate joins without the admin handling their password or making the account for them.
explanations.author: agent

explanations.anchorLabel: User Story 1 - Invite a teammate / Acceptance
explanations.body: Given an admin on the members page: submitting a valid email with the role "Editor" creates a pending invitation and sends a join-link email to that address. When the recipient opens the link while signed out, they are asked to sign in or register, and on success become an Editor of the workspace. If the email already belongs to a member, the repeat invitation is rejected with an "already a member" message.

sources.label: User Story 1 - Invite a teammate / Acceptance

explanations.author: agent

explanations.body: An admin cancels a pending invitation so its link stops admitting anyone — the take-back the constitution requires before an access grant is used.
explanations.author: agent

explanations.anchorLabel: User Story 2 - Revoke an invitation / Acceptance
explanations.body: Given a pending invitation: when the admin revokes it, its status becomes revoked and the join link no longer admits anyone. A recipient who then opens the link is told the invitation is no longer valid and is not added to the workspace.

sources.label: User Story 2 - Revoke an invitation / Acceptance

explanations.anchorLabel: User Story 3 - Invitations expire on their own
explanations.body: An invitation that is never opened stops working after a fixed window (default 7 days), so a forgotten or leaked link cannot be used months later.

explanations.anchorLabel: User Story 3 - Invitations expire on their own / Acceptance
explanations.body: Given an invitation created 8 days ago under a 7-day window: opening its link is refused as expired and no membership is created.

explanations.body: The eight requirements below fix who may create an invitation, how a join link behaves across its whole lifecycle, and what every state change must record.
explanations.author: agent

explanations.body: An admin creates an invitation for one email address with exactly one role drawn from the workspace’s existing role set.
explanations.author: agent

explanations.body: The system emails the invited address a single-use join link bound to that specific invitation.
explanations.author: agent

explanations.body: An invitation is rejected when its email already belongs to a member of the same workspace — you cannot invite someone who is already in.
explanations.author: agent

explanations.body: A join link admits its recipient only while the invitation is pending; accepted, revoked and expired invitations each refuse it.
explanations.author: agent

explanations.body: An admin can revoke a pending invitation, after which its link is refused.
explanations.author: agent

explanations.body: An invitation expires automatically after a window measured from its creation, configurable and defaulting to 7 days.
explanations.author: agent

explanations.body: Every invitation state change — created, accepted, revoked, expired — is written to the audit log with the actor and a timestamp.
explanations.author: agent

explanations.body: Accepting an invitation creates exactly one membership carrying the invitation’s role, even if the link is opened twice — acceptance is idempotent.
explanations.author: agent

explanations.body: The feature rests on four things: a Workspace that owns invitations and memberships; an Invitation holding the target email, offered role, single-use token, status and expiry; a Membership created when an invitation is accepted; and a Role the invitation offers and the membership carries.

glossary.definition: The link emailed to an invited address; it carries the invitation’s token and admits the recipient exactly once, only while the invitation is pending.
glossary.author: agent

glossary.definition: The state an invitation starts in and the only state in which its link admits anyone; accepted, revoked and expired are the terminal states.

diagrams.title: Creating and accepting an invitation
diagrams.mermaid:
%% Invitation: create then accept
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Admin as Admin Browser
  participant API as Harbor API
  participant Mail as Email Service
  participant Invitee as Invitee Browser
  Admin->>API: POST create invitation, email + role
  API->>API: validate role, reject if already a member
  API->>Mail: send single-use join link
  API-->>Admin: pending invitation
  Invitee->>API: GET invitation by token
  API-->>Invitee: accept page if pending and unexpired
  Invitee->>API: POST accept
  API->>API: create one membership, mark accepted
  API-->>Invitee: redirect into workspace
diagrams.trigger: request/response across >=2 named participants (admin, API, email service, invitee)

diagrams.title: Invitation lifecycle

stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> pending: admin creates
  pending --> accepted: invitee joins
  pending --> revoked: admin cancels
  pending --> expired: window passes
  accepted --> [*]
  revoked --> [*]
  expired --> [*]
